ch.h:
“Carrying in his arms, the cold lifeless body of the happiness, with blood on his hands, soiling her dress. His sword pierced in victor’s chest. He walked and walked, into the fanning flame, into the fire, last to be seen at that time by any living eye.”

‘THE END’

“Whew, finally done with my third story.” Sal, with a sigh of relief as he closed down the screen of the laptop. ‘My readers were looking forward to the end, I hope so that it meets their expectations, not to mention, ufff, a tragic end, many won’t be happy.’ Sal got up, drew the curtains, and threw himself on the bed. “My, what a day, writing online novels aint an easy cup of tea, but, I guess the remarks of the readers makes it worth it.” Already tired with fatigue of sitting, Sal was drowsy and quickly dozed off. Tired, exhausted, in that uncomfortable pose was living a comfortable life. A peaceful life. With an innocent face, he slept, not aware of what was in store for him next.

Time waits for none, no one but those who are capable of changing time. The words posted right above his study table. “Just what a son, writing cringy stuff, and posting web novels like a tragic hero.” Looking at her son, who was now covered with a sheet, and in a better pose, she smiled, despite all her complains, cleaning out his room silently. “Mother’s love is beautiful” Sal spoke up, shocked to hear those words with context, she looked behind, yet he was still asleep. Sleep talking. His mother kind of even happy, came close, kissed his forehead, and left the room.

With the creak of the closing door, Sal’s eyes opened. He felt immensely hot, he garbled and got up only to find, his room was on fire. He sprung up on his feet, and quickly ran to the door, in the hallway, which was also on fire. A man stood in between that fire, he was holding Sal’s mother in his arms. Sal froze, he could not move to this sight. The man slowly started walking away, into the fire, last to be ….. With a big thud, that woke Sal up, he realized he was watching a nightmare, and ended up falling off from his bed. He stood up, worried, glanced his room, it was just like he left it. There was no sheet covering him either. He had felt that his mom came to his room, but, there was no sign of it. Panicking, he ran downstairs. “MAMAA!!” he shouted, and suddenly spotting her on the sofa, she was shocked to see him suddenly so loud. Sal came up to her, saw her tears, she was crying. He was already scared as was, this made him even more nervous. He suddenly hugged her, as tight as he could, “Please tell me what’s wrong?”, “Why were you crying?” He sounded more panicked, despite wanting to sound assuring. His mom pointed her finger to the TV, and he found himself made the biggest of fools. Finding a Turkish drama which had just ended, the credits were rolling on the screen. Despite this, Sal also made a sigh, it was sigh of relief. It was okay to be a fool, but at least, things were normal, there was no worries or problems. “You scared the shit out of me, mom!” “But what could I have done, such a good story ended.” She said, while wiping her tears and clearing her throat. “Though, this reminds me, of someone, who dozed off at the wrong time and missed their lunch.” Glancing sternly, she said looking at Sal. She was back to her normal self. Sal, worried and happy as well, was now satisfied with his normal life.

It was nine am in the morning. I woke up. It was a good dream that woke me up, but I still do not remember the dream, as usual. It was the 12th of July today, with the last bits of my summer vacations remaining. Upon the arrival of 24th July, the prison known as school was to begin.

I suddenly heard mom shout downstairs. I ran down again, seeing me, my mom closed the phone. Not wanting to trouble her anymore, I didn’t ask anything. And nothing happened as well. Life continued normal. I was happy. Me and my mom, in our small cute house. As for my father, my mother made it a taboo to not discuss him. I don’t know the reason, but I never bothered my mom, and honestly, I never felt the need to either.

Today, 12 July, a normal day, and yes a normal day, today doesn’t happen to be my birthday, obviously, because my birthday is on 2nd January. Anyways, back to the normal life, I was, and still am pretty good at studies, and there is one thing, people often misunderstand about me, I don’t like anime. I am not interested in some Japanese cartoons with eyes bigger than hotpots. What I do like is, Japanese tech, and interest to some extent in robotics.

Life is passing by and my team to rejoin the prison is nearing, but even as all this passes, I still haven’t forgotten about the dream I had that day.

Now, as much as I want to start off with the caption, *12 Days Later* I will not, because it still is 12th of July. A chief person in my life, has yet to make a call. A person, who made my life, so…., I won’t mention it, because, one never knows, he may well be reading it.

Sal was sitting on the sofa, watching the ticking clock. It was 4:29 and 34 sec. He watched the needle ticked off bit by bit, and as soon as it struck 60, with 4: 30 pm, the phone rang and Sal, picked it up with the blink of an eye. Sal talked for hours, 4 to be precise. They talked on all sorts of things. Coffee, flavors, Game of Thrones, some stupid Urdu novel, some stuff about aroma and nostalgia that Sal nodded to but did not understood in the bit and a lot of other things. With the end of the call, smiling Sal got up, 12 July was officially over.

* 12 Days Later *

My day started with a different routine. It was the routine of the prisoner days. Right now, I was on the road to that very prison. Walking to school is not easy, but I still do it out of the fun and effort. Last night, I read a comment on my story, someone was criticizing me for being a heart broken person and channeling my sorrow to my stories. Which was interesting to read, because, truth be told, I have never experienced any sort of romance or relationships. Though, me not being interested in romance does not mean I don’t like the very idea of it. Rather, I would want to have someone romantic in my company. Now my friend, who doesn’t even like to be referred to as a friend, ( he doesn’t give any alternative either ) he claims to be romantic. But truth be told, his romance is something totally off, and I don’t want to get into an argument on the topic of romanticism, I just simply want to have, in plain words, a plainly flirty person in my company. Having only Saiph, is kinda, heavy.

Shrouded with thoughts like those, I realized I was at the gate of my school already. I made my way up to the classroom. Normally Saiph was already there, but it appears I made it before him today. Despite being the second topper of my class, (First being Saiph) I was not interactive with people, and did not stood out. So, basically without Saiph, I was a loner. My eyes were fixed at the gate from which I expected Saiph to enter any moment. But he did not. The day went on, periods went by yet Saiph did not come. And that day, literally changed to become a real prison to me.

My shoes felt heavy, for a long time, I felt weary and tired. School was over. I realized another thing. It was not school that was the prison, but the loneliness of not having your friend nearby you. On that day, I told myself, a school with Saiph there, would no longer be called a prison. I once again, remembered the comment, ‘You sure are a romantic but heartbroken person.’ I was not romantic, but heck, I was heartbroken at that moment. I couldn’t help but give myself a pitying laugh. On the way, I saw a bench at a waiting stop, I took a moment to collect myself. Saiph did not come for just one day, why the heck do I have to be so serious? Despite knowing, I was fake counselling myself, I wanted to make an effort. Saiph after all, had a big impact on my life. Submerged in these thoughts, a bike stopped in front of me, it was someone from our school, I personally did not recognize him, but he offered me a lift, and to my surprise, I said Yes.

The journey back was silent. Normally I talk to myself, but today, I stayed silent in the mind too. I was becoming overly anxious. I really wanted to see him, and not being able to made me very sad. When I reached home, I dashed for my room. I told my mom I would not take lunch today. She understood that I was upset and decided to give me time by not saying anything at the moment, but damn, was I hungry.

In my room, I went straight for the phone. Dialed Saiph’s number. It came of as powered off. I called his landline, to which there was no response. Now, as a writer myself, this was no less than the most climatic and worrisome moment for the character. The numbers to which I always received the quickest of responses were now all unresponsive. I decided to call his mother. I had memorized her number, but had not saved it. It was ringing, and it finally connected. But to my dismay, the one who responded was not Saiph’s mother, it was his dad.

‘Why? I thought to myself. Why did he pick up the phone? Wasn’t, he supposed to be abroad. Why is he here? All these questions flooded me as I tried to speak. “Uncle, I am Saiph’s friend, I am worried for him, he did not come to school today, May I, Can I talk to him?” My voice was grave, I knew something was off. “Son, Saiph won’t be coming to school for a while…” His voice was down, and, hearing him say what he said, my phone literally would have dropped to the ground had this been a drama, but with the grasp of reality, my gripped on the phone tightened as well. “Why” I put all my intense emotion into this one word while staying as respectful as possible. I heard him say in quavering voice, “Saiph, a couple of days ago, suddenly collapsed, we rushed him to the hospital, and there appears to be a blood clot in his brain, …” I was sure that his dad was crying silent tears by now. “His condition is critical, the doctors told us, that the surgery is very complex, and chancing of success here are very low, they recommended us to take him abroad if possible, So I sent his mother along with him to USA, I myself will be going tomorrow too. Son, PLEASE PRAY.” It was as if he was pleading, as if my prayer could really save him, the least I could do was, assure him, I was crying myself, but I said as sternly as possible, “I WILL.”

Had my phone dropped now, it wouldn’t have been that dramatic, for like the gravity that will pull the phone down, the gravity of the situation was equally serious.

There were 2 people, only two people in my life, that were dear to me, dear enough more than my own existence. My mom and Saiph. I never gave a damn about anyone else, but this meant that I gave all the damn to these two.

On my bed, I was laying, thinking, about the only word that had filled my mind. ‘Saiph.’ I picked up my phone, opened up the recorder, there was one saved file named Saiph. I clicked on it. “Hahaha, what are you doing, close it. What do you even want me to say?” “Anything” this was my voice, it was so full of life, for a moment I could even believe that it was someone else, such was the type of person I am. “Try reading Pir-e-Kamil.” I said. After that I heard on my phone, Saiph read a paragraph from that book.

It was the only source of Saiph’s voice I had at hand. Hearing it, I couldn’t help but cry again. And slowly knowing and learning more about the type of person I was myself.

I heard a knock on the door. “Sal, would you be coming to dinner?” I heard mom’s voice. Honestly, I did not want to, but I had skipped lunch too, and I was damn hungry now. Life is cruel, almost as if forcing you to live, even when you don’t have any desire too. “Coming...” I replied.

It was dinner, there was silence. An unusual silence. “Is there anything bothering you?” My mom paved way for me to speak up. “Yes” I replied. “What can I do for you then?” she added. “Send me to America.” Her spoon stopped midway, she took a moment to collect herself from this unexpected response and asked me why. I ended up telling her the whole situation.

“Sal boy, I understand your feeling now, but, even you know the answer to your question. I won’t blame you from where you are coming, but, we cannot do anything, so at least. Pray.” My mom got up, patted me on my head. I kept sitting on my chair, thinking about my helplessness. Unfortunately, my mother was right. The reality kept gnawing at me more and more, bit by bit.

I really am a weak person and emotional person. I cannot face up or stand to challenges. I realized a big flaw about myself. 10 days had past. I was still disturbed. It was 3rd August, and I had taken a leave from school, as well as from my online writing. My days went by with me doing nothing, except praying at times, for Saiph, but seeing my condition, I doubt I was able to do that with sincerity.

It was at a time like this that I was sitting idle when the doorbell rang. It was someone from the delivery service. He handed me a letter, which has Saiph’s father’s name on top of it. I quickly signed and brought it inside and opened the package. Inside was the real thing, with the writing, that I could have recognized anywhere. “Royal Post Universal Mailing Service, R.U.M.S” It was the thing me and Saiph came up with whenever we passed each other our notes. By now, my hands were shivering, and my eyes were teary.

“There was no salutation as expected. And the letter started.

‘I’ll not mention the timing, but I am in a cold room in a cold land but I have peace right now because of the Salistic moment which is cliché, but I’m glad I got the chance to write. My soul-ful Sal, I won’t say anything about my condition at the moment, but let me tell you, I am proud of you, and don’t let it get you down and Je t’ Aime.

I wanted to call you after 12th but I did not, honestly, I kind of regret that. My head doesn’t seem to be working properly, but today, I knock at your door to confess, I really love you my dear dear Sal. I really do not want to lose you, but looking at myself, the situation points otherwise.

I am sure my every act had a complain, and I expressed it because I knew it was for the right one and I know you got me and I know you will get me now too.

Sal, live your aroma, enjoy your flavors and make it so you take my presence along with you. For that would be endless bliss for me, and if you ever miss me, just look at the cat. I always knew you loved them, so look at ‘babu’ ( I already took the liberty of naming the cat ) and remember me in good memories and don’t ever let it take you down.

I BID YOU STRENGTH

De ton speculo,
Karagami Saiph.”

That was all.

Silence followed, even the cat stayed still as if mimicking a stuff toy.

But “A soundless space is like honey to bees” hence at the passing of a few seconds, the whimpering sounds of my tears and sobbing filled the space.

4 August

I got ready for prison (school) with confidence. Yesterday’s letter had a really positive impact on me. I had decided to face my problems, for Saiph’s sake. I offered my prayer and recited my Quran as usual. Ate my breakfast and went on my way.

I made sure I didn’t forget my bag today.

The cat had gotten attached to me and my mom in just 1 day. She was a calm and collected animal, a lot like someone who I decided to change myself for.

I used my bicycle to commute and was able to reach on time. A little early actually. Got the luxury to choose a window seat and that made me thinking about my concept for the new novel that I should start writing. Nothing special came to mind and the class started slowly after.

It was my second day in 11 grade, a few of the other boys tried to initiate conversation but I showed no interest. The teacher after setting some of his files at the table looked at us to garner our attention. “We will be having another new comer join us today, and you know the drill, be nice.” “He has joined us from New Zealand so be sure to guide him for the setup is new and all.”

A good looking boy stepped into the class, he was Pakistani by origin so not a native New Zealand person.

“Assalumalikum, my name is Rajeel, nice to meet you all.”

He introduced himself with the first name only, I personally found it a bit strange. I also noticed he was wearing a name badge on his shirt’s left side captioned “ SATSU “
God knows what that meant but it surely felt weird as to why.

He had a familiar looking face to me as if I had seen it somewhere but at the same time I was quite sure I was seeing this boy for the first time in my life.

He glanced all around, as if he was scanning everything but it stopped when his eyes met mine. At that moment a cold shiver went down my spine. A strong urge of having Saiph along with me was given birth too.

“Can I sit there?” pointing towards the empty chair besides me, he asked the teacher. “Go on” said the teacher. He approached the seat in a manner that personally felt intimidating to my existence.
“Can you move your bag, sir” pointing towards my bag on the seat, he requested posing to be a gentleman which kind of annoyed me. “what’s with the formal tone? Are you a fallen English prince?” I remarked cynically. “I like to approach things, especially new, with a gentle behavior.” He replied with a smirk. “well sorry, this seat belongs to Saiph. You cannot sit here.” I declared.

The whole class was dead silence. The teacher rather astonished too, but before anyone could speak, He picked my bag “I don’t know who this Saiph is, but you will have to excuse me.” Putting the bag at the side, and took the chair for himself. His tone this time around was rather bitter.

The feel of anger and fury, the urge to punch him welled inside me but aware of my weak stature, I was forced to refrain from blockbuster action. I could finally feel my normal life going away into the distant lands.

A few moments had passed, class had resumed and Rajeel leaned a little close to me, whispering into my ear, “It’s going to be a spicy year, I’m looking forward now”. I looked at him to saw him giving me a mean smile. It did not felt good.

What is love? Me and Saiph used to debate a lot. It was my view that we both weren’t very romantic people. Actually we aren’t at all. Saiph thought otherwise though. But to me, being romantic felt as if it refers to physically carrying out love. Romanticism and love felt two different entities. And one can still understand and talk about love without being romantic himself.

For Saiph, Love was nothing. Perhaps in his view, he pictured it as vacuum waiting to be filled with an abstract art of feelings which could be named love. Maybe it was something else. I never really understood but he would always negate the notion of a definition of love. To him it was ‘nothing’. He even said marriage is a pact and has nothing to do with love. To me that sounds heretic. But then, im forced to think, what love might be for me. I am no philosopher but to me, love feels like a tool to transcend norms, definitions and boundaries. Everyone has their own way of love. But one thing was certain, a lover radiates an energy which emits positivity not only to the lover but to everyone around them. It felt more like a super power. Those who love, make others feel a force, have them experience emotions that they have never felt prior.

Perhaps these thoughts might make my definition closer to Saiph’s but surely the way I perceive it is different. My urge to understand love is as equal as my urge to fall in love with it, and be a lover for it is love that makes us the crown of creation.

Thinking and narrating thoughts about love in my head, I realized I lost sense of time and had already reached home. I stepped inside and noticed we had a guest. When I went to greet him, I saw a foreigner probably in his forty’s. It was an uneasy awkward feeling but a lot of questions pondered my mind.

Assalumialikum, he said. I greeted back. I thought to myself that he probably was a Muslim the way he greeted. I saw Babu purring along his legs as if he was family. I gave a look of question to my mom but weirdly she had gone all white, as if she had seen a ghost. Perhaps it was because I had stepped into their conversation which they might not have wanted me to pry on. The man was smiling though. He radiated a very warm and comforting aura. But to avoid being a burden, I said my excuses and went upstairs to my room.

Sitting on my ‘Thinking Chair’ which was the chair I used to think and write my stories on, I started thinking, about my own life as a story. I was really curious about who the man was and what they were talking about.

I was thinking about different things like Saiph and my own personality when I heard a call from my mom. Apparently the guest was leaving and wanted to see me. I stepped down, saw him wearing a sad smile. If I was not wrong, maybe his eyes were a little watery too. He did not say anything and just patted my shoulder and took his leave. I turned behind to see mom also crying silent tears. Holding back sorrows that I perhaps was not ready to face. It took me a moment to realize and connect all the dots in my head but it finally clicked. The man who just left was the man who came in my dream. He was the ONE.

I called at my mother, asking her the question I perhaps was scared of facing all along. “He was my father wasn’t he?”

And a reply that was out there was given to me. YES!

It was years ago … my mother sat me down in the hallway and the story was finally about to be delivered. She continued …

“My twin sister Talia and I, in our twenties’ young blood and all, always out to explore things. It was a day like that, during our part time job at a Mc Donald’s chain that we finally decided to confront him.

Every evening this young gentleman would come there at a specific time. We used to observe him daily because he stood out from among the crowd. Obviously he would. He was a foreigner.

Apparently he moved in from New Zealand just 1 month ago. He was a recently converted Muslim and spoke some of the cutest Urdu we had ever heard. Talia used his Urdu as an excuse to talk to him, offering that she can help him with it. Poor guy did not understand that she just wanted to have some play time by hearing him is all.

Skipping all the details, within a year that passed by quick, something that started as a tease developed into a full fledge romance and the best thing to her luck was that it was mutual. He too, had developed quite a fondness for her. I saw it coming and knew I would not be able to beat my overwhelming sister so I had kept myself as the back seat passenger to it all to avoid being a hurdle.

Brendon was a devout Muslim but he still preferred western names so he did not change his’. Considering marriage to be the proper way, Talia and Brendon got engaged and the preparations for marriage underway.

He had a good job, a good character so our family had no issues despite him being a foreigner. The wedding date was about to be set that Talia suddenly got selected for a short and very important course regarding her degree that only a few chosen students are selected for. She had been wanting and trying her best for this so understanding the situation, the family put a halt on all the functional preparation, and since it was only a small tenure, 2 weeks, the date was set to 2 weeks after in accordance to her arrival. Invitations were half way sent so all the guests and the remaining guests were given an update on the new situation and timings.

2 weeks went by pretty quick and Talia and Brendon were both excited for each other. It was her last day and she was supposed to come back tomorrow. Venting their excitements, the day passed and came the day where she was to come back.
Weirdly, she was not picking up any calls that day. We all thought she would be busy or perhaps wanting to give a surprise. Everyone was worried but they all had pinned their hopes on optimistic events in mirror to Talia’s optimistic personality. The day went by. The last flight for that day from UK came. Talia’s whereabouts were unknown.

“Time does not stop

And it kept running”

A whole week had gone by. All services and involved organizations were contacted and asked help from. The university tried to avoid taking the blame saying she never came to them and had gone off somewhere. The corporation that had hosted the event and the hotel where she stayed all said she signed off as per schedule. The police tried but could not sniff out her routes. The course organizer said that she was to meet them at a location to rendezvous to the airport but she never made it on time.

Everything that was possible was tried. Time had gone by. The whole family and marriage preparation left as was.

How Talia would dream and joke of knights coming to swoop her on their horse, but today, the knight and horse were both there, but she herself wasn’t. After a deliberation of thoughts by the elders, it was decided that the marriage will continue.

It came as a shock to Brendon and even so for me. The idea was dumb because I was being used as a scapegoat. I asked him to voice against this decision but in foreign lands, in despair, he didn’t say a single thing. The game had already gone out of hand.

I tried my best but life threw me in the exact cliché Pakistani drama situation that one could find on any serial drama channel. And with that, in the coming, driest and dead days of my life, I found myself as Mrs. Brendon.

It’s not as if he was a bad guy. On the first night after the marriage, he apologized for being weak, and also apologized for not being a proper husband in times a woman fantasies the most. I could understand because Talia was my sister too. He said, he will try his best to run this relationship but he will always wait for Talia. He had not given up and his answer was final for him.

Life went on. It was very sweet. I could not feel the emotion of love from within but the amount of care and respect alone made me feel so special. That was love for me. Surprisingly, with time, all the bitter memories started to fade and I had moved on from the past, and finally settled in with my current way of life.

After two years, we had a child. He named him Sal. Yes, that was you. With your birth, the emotion I had felt he was missing all along finally became the last piece of the puzzle that fitted in. and now, I felt as if he had indeed moved on from Talia. It was a selfish thought for me but somewhere at the back of my head, the words he told me at the first night had spewed a seed of insecurity.
But son, remember this, “negativity is just an adrenaline boost to a crippled body. Eventually it falls.”

One phone call, destroyed my fantasy house. It was Talia.

Talia was found in France. Apparently, there were many kidnappings of non-English native people around the time of Talia’s kidnapping. The police were hell bent on busting out this black market for human trafficking. Eventually they caught a lead on the trail of this mafia group and blew their chain of system. They then discovered how vast the system had already spread and it took them time to follow up on the cases.

One of those routes eventually led to the raids on different hideouts in other European countries. With a combined support, and time. Eventually manly girls were saved. Talia was one of them. She was found in a nearly devastated state and apparently succumbed to a state of coma for 3 months. With no information on her with the government of France, they treated her and eventually with the paper work done between France and Britain, they discovered and linked her to the lost missing student from Pakistan. During this time, Talia had regained consciousness and her family, that means us, were informed.

She had been raped countless of times, mistreated like an inhuman thing. She had even been hurt to the extent that she had lost her ability to walk. The Talia, that came back, sitting on the wheelchair was a dead corpse.

Brendon later told me that he wants to live with her. Seeing Talia, I could only pity her. I too felt bad for her and willingly told him that yes he should go and tend to her. I offered him that there was an option for us both to look after her but Brendon said that looking at us would only affect her more mentally because this was the life she was supposed to live. Those words stinged a little but they were understandable.

We had a healthy divorce. He then married her and relocated back to New Zealand for a better environment aimed at her rehabilitation.

Brendon never failed to send money ever since that day. He felt bad for leaving his son but he knew he could not care for both his wife and son in that situation. For Talia, he said, it was important to start anew.

We had no contact. It was probably due to me, and he realized it and never crossed that boundary. Every month a certain amount would come to my bank and that was it. Life went on like this until today when there was a knock on the door and he stood still looking almost the same.

The later part of the story that I wasn’t aware of, was now told to me by him.

Apparently, Talia and them had a good start. With time and care by Brendon, Talia started to recover quicker than was anticipated. Things started to get better and they even had a kid down the line. You were a few months when he left so there would be around 2 years of age difference.

Life kinda settled in for them. Talia was pretty strong to have been recovering but, I have no idea why, life had already been enough of a punishment for them then why …

There was an accident. Lightning struck down the place where they lived. A pole fell down and since it struck near their house. There was a fire and a blast. Their house collapsed and unfortunately Talia could not survive. Since she was crippled. Brendon was only able to save their son.

Time was hard on them, eventually Brendon came to Pakistan and raised his son alone. Being in New Zealand made him feel too alone. Yet he still did not contact me because it would have been unfair for him to use me now that he had lost Talia. He tried his best.

But the story does not end here. Eventually down the line, Brendon was diagnosed with cancer. He fought to the best of his abilities. But it was futile for him. He was already in his last stages.

That’s why he came to me today. To let me know, and request me to please take in his son. He had told him about me from day one so his son would not be a bother. He said stuff here and there as to how he won’t be a bother but it still made me feel very hurt. Why did he not come to me? What is wrong with humans making life difficult for themselves in the name of formalities.

Brendon did not cry when Talia went missing. He did not cry when he saw Talia in such a miserable state, yet today, he was crying, apologizing for everything and asking me to take his son in. And what could I have done. I accepted!

My mother spoke her last words “I accepted”. She was crying and I too had teared up. I hugged my mother and told her, it will be alright. We will overcome any challenge together like always. Saying that, I gave her a hand to help her stand up. Asked her to go and take a nap to freshen and relax the mind. She followed and I too went on to my room to lay down for indeed fourth of august had been a heavy day.

One thing that I realized was, the dream I had that day, it was not my mother in it but her twin sister Talia. And that the dream was a sign of something that was to come.
***

4 days had past. I was getting ready for prison as per routine that the phone rang. It was the eight of august and I will never forget this day for it was ‘Saiph’.
The operation was a success and yes, Saiph was alive and well. Saiph was coming back he said. The amount of euphoria was unattainable. It was so good that it started feeling unreal.

I forgot about the school and kept talking to him for hours catching up on things from his end. He told me how he will return on 10 august. I was so excited for it. But this excitement made me forget, to every reaction, there is an equal but opposite reaction.

10th august, the news was on. I was standing like a statue.

Flight E-A90 of Blue Airways on its way from Washington had crashed in the Indian Ocean. Till now, operations of rescue were ongoing but no survivors have been confirmed.

The only word I could utter to from my dry stoned mouth at that time was
“Saiph”

My eyes opened, I wiped them off for I realized I had been crying. I looked at the calendar. It was the ninth of august. ‘I dream’ I realized although it was no consolation for once again it felt like a sign like my previous dream.

I had no way of contacting Saiph because I could not place international calls. It was a very uneasy feeling in the middle of the night at 3:43 am. Helpless, I tried to sleep but could not properly.

Time went on though ….
I found myself in school. The Rajeel guy was not present. He was not very punctual and even the days he did came previously, nothing special happened. The first class went by and everything felt normal. It was during the second class that we all saw Rajeel at the entrance of the class. He looked pale, and very anxious but he was trying his best to stay collected. He silently came and sat beside me. I did not bother him this time. He stayed silent all throughout the rest of the classes, lost in thought. Obviously something was wrong but no one felt it appropriate to pry in. It felt as if there was a strong wall to cross to ask him what was wrong.

Soon, it was recess time. Everyone indulged in their activities. I was focused at him until he looked at me and asked, “Had a nightmare?” at first I thought he was stating but it was him actually asking me. “Damn, how did you know?” I blurted out.

With a giggle of laughter, he said that it was all over my face. Seeing him smile somehow made me feel less anxious. “Tell me then, what was your nightmare about?” he asked. Despite all that was going, his voice felt rather compelling. And I let him know what my best friend was going through and how I had a dream about him.

“Is that best friend called Saiph? You used his name when defending this chair.” He asked. I was surprised he remembered but I affirmed. “I too had a good friend named Saif once. Look out for your friend. Pray for him.”

He then added, “I also have a solution for your problem, but as payment you will let me come to your home.” Not even Saiph had been to my home yet so I felt reluctant but the idea in itself did not feel bad enough so I said OK. He then later on went to his state of pondering again, lost in thought but yet again I couldn’t ask what was wrong.

It was finally pack up time, and picking our stuff up, we both were on our way to my home. Since I used to commute on a bicycle, and weirdly he was on foot, we both decided to walk while towing my cycle along the way.

Making little conversation, in due time, we reached. “So this is your home. Pretty cozy looking.” He said. To me it felt a superficial compliment that people do to keep heart.

“So how can u help me?” I asked without beating around the bush. “Do you have his number?” he asked back. “I cannot place international calls, if I could, I would have already done that. But yes, I have his number”.

He took the number, and then took his phone out from his bag. Mobile phones were not allowed in school yet he still had it. Dialing the number, he passed the phone to me. “My phone can make International calls.” He smiled.

The call was answered by Saiph’s family and they told me all was well. It made me relax and Rajeel did what he said he would. “Why did you come to my house for this though? Could you not have done this in school or on the way?”

“Haha, I could have but I wanted to see your house. Call it my curiosity for personal feelings.” He said. At this stage, New Zealand, the way Rajeel looked, the timing, his words, … my mind did indeed make its own weird theories, but I did not want to accept them so I kept them blocked out.

Another weird thing was that my mom was supposed to be at home but she was not. I looked for my mobile which was powered off, so I turned it on. 19 missed call by ‘mom’ I saw. Worried, I called back. “what’s wrong I asked?” and in a cold voice she replied, “Its your father. He …”

I was almost running in the corridors of the ‘City Hospital’ searching for my mom. Rajeel was with me. He insisted on coming and I did not have the luxury to stop him.
I finally found her. She seemed as if she was crying but she actually was not. “what happed to him?” I asked. “He died during the night at 3:43 am” she spoke gravely looking down at the floor in a voice that echoed despair.

The floor from under my feet felt as if it had disappeared. I felt dizzy with the pressure of my own thoughts crushing me. That time. It was the same time I had woken up due to that nightmare.

My mother did not look up and for some reason I had no energy left to stay there so I silently left. Rajeel followed along behind me.

“are you sure it was okay to leave without saying anything?” he asked.
I had no energy to reply so I just looked at him and stayed silent. He too did not ask anything after that. We parted ways to each our way. I reached home where silence awaited me. A creepy feeling that made me feel as if my soul was being drained.

It was 11th August. Saiph contacted me and said they had rescheduled their flight just as a precaution. Which helped because coincidently, during a preflight inspection, they found some doubtful problems so the flight was cancelled. Saiph said their new flight was on 12th August now. I was happy but too much had happened for me to be able to sort and express my feelings properly. We had a heartfelt talk about different things. It felt a little comforting.

Today was also the funeral of Brendon. My dad. He had wished to be buried in New Zealand along with Talia. My mom also went to attend it. I was not allowed though.

I did not have the energy to go to school so I was staying back at home. The same thing happened the next day too. My mom’s flight was to be inbound today near noon, while Saiph’s was to be there at night.

I was also told that my supposed step brother would also be in tow with my mom on her way back.

Drifting in my thoughts, I killed time eventually having heard the bell rung. It was probably my mother given the time. I could not go receive her at the airport as she told me to stay at home. It was her way of giving me time to relax and cool down. I went on and opened the door, to see my mom and Rajeel standing side by side.

I would not say it was not expected. But this guy was hanging around with me at times he was supposed to be there. That was a big factor that made me hope my theories were wrong and everything I saw was a mere coincidence. I knew he looked a little younger than me too and probably had skipped grades but my mind was bent on not believing it. Yet there he stood. Despite knowing, I still asked, “Why and what are you doing here with my mom?” My mother made her way in ignoring my question and us. She clearly had her own demons to fight and was told everything by Rajeel along the way. She did not waste time with us. On the other hand, Rajeel kept standing at the door and only gave me a broken smile as a response to my question.

“I told you it would be a spicy year, I told you that didn’t I” he followed up after a moments pause. All the mix of feelings inside me made me want to blow up. I punched the door and went upstairs.

After a few hours, he came to me in my room. “Why are you so angry?” he asked.

“The day your father died, you were hanging out with me, why?” I asked him. He was late to school that day. He was lost in thought and looked pale. All the dots connected.
“Why you asked, is it not obvious? My father had died. Was there anything I could do? No! the day was to come. I knew, but still, it was not easy. You think I came to this school and class without knowing who you were? I knew, and that is why, I tried to seek solace with you. As you were having the same blood. The idea made me feel less alone. In simple words, I was just running away from my own life.”

I felt bad, hearing him put it out like this in the open. He almost teared up when saying it all. I stood up and hugged him. “I will try my best to be family” I said. “Thank you” was his response. For once, I felt as if I was above him in the situation and in control. It was a nice feeling.

My life had indeed taken a 360O turn. I was now an older brother. I had not told Saiph of Rajeel to keep him stress free until he came back so I was kind of excited to share it all with him tomorrow. I was excited to have him meet Rajeel. I had a feeling, the three of us could be a good trio of friends.

13th August, I went to school with Rajeel. I saw Saiph. It felt like ages and hence could not control my urge to hug him. Seeing him healthy made me so happy. I quickly turned over to introduce to Saiph to Rajeel but to my dismay, I saw Rajeel standing white as if he had seen a ghost.
Saiph stood there with similar expressions, both of them silent. It was Rajeel who broke the silence. “Well, hello there, BROTHER Saiph. Long time no see.” He said it in a very mean tone.

Diverting his attention to me he said, “I don’t want to spoil your reunion with Saif so I shall be going ahead.” Having said that, he went and sat on the opposite side of the classroom. He clearly looked upset. Neither me nor Saiph could say anything and we just sat together silently. There was no reunion.

During recess, I informed Saiph of the whole story. How and who Rajeel was and what he was doing in my life. It took me the whole of recess to explain him the situation. Time went on and so did the classes and I could not ask from him about Rajeel. I wanted to ask Saiph. After school, Saiph got up and tried to leave but I held his arm. “You aren’t going anywhere” “No buts” I was stubborn.

Rajeel winked at me and showed me a good luck sign as he went out. Saiph and I both got seated in the empty class and he began the tale …

I came to this college in ninth, before that I never shared but I was in city school. Saiph was telling about himself. Saiph had vaguely mentioned about his past but never in detail. I guess Rajeel was the reason. Saiph went on …

“I told you I never truly had someone to call a friend. In the past, I had someone but after ‘that’ happened, I was forced to change my perception.

We were really close since grade 5. I discovered a boy who had lost his mother and came to Pakistan, new to the whole system. A boy who felt unique. Our time went amazing. 2 years of golden time. But then came the unlucky seventh.

Back in the days Saiph had told me that seventh and eighth grades were his worst schooling experiences. I was finally going to know why!

Saiph continued, ... during all this time, I was aware of all his interests. He had this delusional concept of being the king of Saturn. People would laugh at him but still feel attracted to that absurdness of his. He was also in love with this form of media called ‘anime” some Japanese cartoon sort of things. He would always go around saying he was a proud Otaku. He obviously loved japan too because of that. His love for anime was a tad bit abnormal I would say. He was relatively good in studies too though not the best, and yes, he loved animals a lot. Like a lot.

He was good at socializing. He was also skilled at getting people to like him, but one thing that was stuck within his heart like a burning desire was the need to be in love. The romantic kind. It was not his age but he wanted a love partner, a promised one.

While Saiph kept on going, I thought to myself how little I knew of my own brother. “It was exactly this love thing that destroyed it all.” Saiph said.

It was ‘City School’. A renowned school where mostly brats from rich families would come. Evil and cringe people were a common day sighting. The school was co-ed. There was this girl called Kamilla. Her real name was Ma… let’s just stick Kamilla for the sake of privacy, sorry.

So anyways, she was this pretty famous girl throughout the school. Despite being kids, many children did get intimate with each other and it was very disgusting to me to be honest. Time went on but she did not take any direct action until one day, she handed a letter to Rajeel after classes. After that Rajeel spent quite a lot of time and exchanged a lot of letter. All I could do was keep an eye then one I saw them, they were holding hands and by god they looked so stupid. Now it was time for me to move . But how?

I contacted my cousin Saba, she’s a super non serious person but if situation calls, she can be reliable a lot. Time went by, I am not sure but I believe they might even have kissed, eww, 7 grade was about to end, I still tried explaining it to him but he said ‘even if you are right, I can and will change her’ poor boy, he didn’t know toys can’t save their masters and that he was a toy. To save him, for his better it was time to make jokes a reality I knew I would have suffered too but for Rajeel.

It was recess, and the chance that I was waiting for presented itself. I found Kamilla in the corridors alone. I pounced at her but surprisingly she was quick and guarded herself. The teachers made their way and the scene that was presented to them was that of her hitting and assaulting me because obviously my shirt was losing button with all her jerking me around. Rajeel upon hearing the news could not believe Kamilla doing such a thing, he without a moment of thought or regard to our friendship blamed me as the perpetrator. He tried his best to defend Kamilla in front of the authorities but who listens to a child.

I had a reputation for being a docile and intelligent, respectable student and the teachers favored me over her in all means. I felt guilty that I somehow was pardoned but Kamilla was expelled. I felt a relief that things would settle down but little had I known that the so called friend would turn from a puppet to her into a monster who will ruin my life. He even threatened me to stay away from him or he will beat me into a pulp. Nothing of what I said could have done anything after that. I realized the extent of our friendship was just an overestimated idealization on my personal behalf. I lose hope in friends until obviously I met you Sal.

The guilt and sad feelings that were swelling up within my heart quelled down. I had stopped caring.

In the next grade, 8 class, Rajeel who had a little social influence managed to outcast me and label me. The other kids even if they too did not like Kamilla scorned me just because I was involved in the incident and different other rumors started. It was sort of bullying. Now Rajeel suddenly came out of nowhere, after 3 whole years, looking and feeling like a totally different person. But he still felt cold. And I’m sure he hates me even now but I don’t care. He is no longer any different from all the normies out there.

I don’t know what his story is for the missing 3 years but I don’t care either!

Since Saiph’s van had gone, we walked home talking on different things. I tried to avoid the topic of Rajeel as much as possible.

At home, I thought on Rajeel’s past and somehow none of them seemed guilty. I had a feeling that I could do something so I made my way to Rajeel’s room.

There he was sitting in his room covered in anime posters and anime stuff here and there. It made me think, Saiph was wrong when he said his love for anime was too much, it was even far more than that level. It was abnormal.

“would you like something of your little brother?” he remarked.
and by God, I had no idea why but I straight ahead went and asked, “Did you and Kamilla kissed back in middle school?”

Hearing the question, he busted into laughter. His weird laugh had a very uneasy vibe to it and I could not pin point if he was amused or laughing to vent of anger for someone prying into his past. Either ways, it was making me uncomfortable.

“That was quite unexpected of you. But now I can assume that Saiph shared his past with you. Not to mention in quite elaborate details haha. Mind sharing with me too, as to what he told you.

That last line felt like shock to my brain because obviously there was something wrong here. “What do you mean by ‘yet’?” I asked.

“It means we haven’t but we might in the coming future obviously.” He spoke in a solemn tone.

Something felt so quenching at my heart. It made my chest so uncomfortably tight for some reason. Even though I had nothing to do with it all. “I thought she was expelled!” I added.

“Oh she surely was, no thanks to Saiph. But, since Saiph dropped out in 8th grade, he wouldn’t know. I also dropped out after 8th. Seeing how much Saiph suffered, and went through for the sake of friendship, all for nothing. This man threw his sacrifice in the fire. Unlike a moment ago where I was trying to decide who could have been wrong in what way, I now could totally see that Rajeel was someone who never had the makings of a loyal friend. I felt enraged. And hence I left the room. He too did not follow.

It was on my sitting chair that all these pestering thoughts kept flooding my head. To regain some composure, I decided to get back to writing my story. My story writing had gone rather slow due to all these twists popping up in my life.

Rajeel started,

Saiph on the other hand, is having it worse. Doctors say the blot clot has sort of partially resurfaced, and this is causing blood flow to be irregular which is somehow causing his Hippocampus to malfunction in turn disrupting the whole bodies homeostasis and temperature.

His temperature cannot be cured and is becoming very hard to regulate even with external help. Doctors say it will only get worse. I could only think to myself. “why now of all times?”

Saiph was conscious and could have visitors but his condition isn’t all too good. I was with him in the hospital while Sal was at home. I was standing in the doorway to his room. Seeing almost made me cry partially cause of his situation and partially cause of guilt for having betrayed him once. I noticed that he had not realized it was me. I sat on the chair besides his bed. Took his hand. “Saiph” I said. My eyes almost watered. He acted as if he was sleeping. Perhaps he was. Or maybe he was still ignoring me. Regardless of that all, with tears dripping my eyes. I told Saiph everything with as honesty as I could that happened. Everything that Kamila was supposed to tell him. But instead it turned out to be me myself having to face my demons. I cried a lot, trying to regain composure but it was turning out to be difficult. In the end, like everyone else, all I said was, “Im sorry”.

The hand in my hand suddenly tightened its grip around mine. He turned his face towards the ceiling and I saw tears were in his eyes too. He then looked at me and told me to come a little near. Clearly he was lacking energy but he spoke in my ears in a graceful soft manner, “You are forgiven”.

The words hit all my worries like an arrow. Swooping them away. That day, I felt one of my ghosts let go of me. I felt more free of my past and guilt and ready to accept what comes next.

That day, I slept in a very uncomfortable pose, in a rather uncomfortable chair, yet I slept assured and sound, knowing I had regained my lost friend for indeed, his hand in mine was a reality.

I had stopped counting days. I was sitting in the waiting area of the hospital. Sal came in through the entrance. I saw him coming towards me. Upon reaching he asked with a stoic look, “you told him?” To which I simply nodded. I was feeling exhausted.

“Why do you look so down then? Shouldn’t you be happy? Now that you got your friend back, a good future awaits.” He said. This made me snap. “Oh really?” I said sarcastically, “Has Dr Sal discovered some cure now that ….” I did not finish the sentence and got hold of my temper. It was unbecoming of me. I looked at Sal again to saw him giving me a smile. A smile of assurance I had never seen on his face before.

“Yes, a cure I have found.” Is what he said.

That night, I had the same dream again. One which has been coming to me in different forms now. Me and Saiph, adults in a big castle. This time, I was giving him a crown, and chants of ‘All hail king Saiph’ would surround us. And just when Saiph would want to say something, I would end waking up. I got up, took a shower and made my way to the hospital. Today was the day we were supposed to carry out the ‘cure’. I could not believe myself we were doing this. I was against it but I could not change Sal’s mind.

It was the same room where I had slept a liberating sleep days ago. And just like that, Saiph was sleeping soundly with heavy breaths though. Sal stood beside the bed. There was a sofa at the corner of the room. That’s where I went and sat.

Sal started circling around the bed. He went around 3 times and came to the exact same spot where he was previously standing. He gazed up. To me where it looked like a simple ceiling yet to him, I’m sure he was looking at something deeper. After a moment of silken and gazing, he said, “I take all of his suffering, tensions, diseases. I take it. I take it. I take it.” Saying that, Sal went into prostration.

To me it looked cheesy. Yet I was going around. Sal stayed in that position for a while and somehow I did not want to watch anymore so I went out of the room to keep guard.

“The Mughal emperor Babur, had a son named Humayun. In his reign, Humayun got severely ill. Babur tried everything but nothing was to his avail. Then one day, an elder told him. “If you really love him more than your life, you can save him. BY proving you do. B putting your life on stake for his.” The Mughal emperor started praying to God to give him all of his kid’s suffering and diseases, just give him health. And eventually Babur got severely ill too. On the other hand, Humayun started to show signs of recovery. Down the line, Babur died of illness. And Humayun would grow up to take reign of his father’s kingdom.”

This was the story Sal told me. “I know they had a father and son bond. I know the story might be dramatized, But I also know my care for Saiph goes beyond my care for my own life. IT might sound cheesy but with belief I know it is possible. I will do this.” Sal was determined. I personally felt dumb hearing all this because it would not really change anything so I decided to let Sal do his thing. But never had I imagined, it would actually work.

Over the course of days, Sal started getting ill. It really scared me. Sal on the other hand would smile ever happily. Doctors could not diagnose any visible problems with Sal. At the very same time, Saiph started to show signs of recovery too.

I would have been happy to have my old friend back but I was not willing to lose my brother for it. I prayed a lot for Sal to get well but to no avail, until eventually, Sal went into a slumber while Saiph was scheduled to a miraculous recovery and being discharged soon. It happened all too quick. Too quick for my brain to understand. I was hit with a severe depression attack these days. My mother and everyone on the loss of Sal were too grave. Saiph though I suppose was not aware of what had happened. I did not leave my room. I even asked Kamilla to leave me alone for a while. I knew, time would help me forget the feeling of my anxiety and helplessness. And it did. In the end, I knew Sal’s name won’t be going down in the history books like Babur, but his love was no less than any. He was proof for me, that real love existed and it did not have to romantic. It is simple devotion that is selfless.

Saiph’s parents were undoubtedly very happy. Throughout this time, they went through a harsh experience. Little they had known that the savior was no longer in this world for them to thank too. When I went to meet Saiph, a long while had passed. It was the day of discharge. He was quite annoyed. He looked at me when I entered. “Where is Sal? Why won’t anyone tell me when I ask a simple question?” Clearly he was being stalled for far too long and now had already started to doubt the worst.

For some reason that day, his eyes looked a lot like Sal’s. I said, “Sal has gone to visit his father in New Zealand.” Saiph gave me a very confused look, but before he could process, I passed him a letter. He opened it up quickly and began to read. For everything else could wait.

My Saiph,

If you are reading this, which I am sure you are, then congratulations. We have made History. Perhaps ours won’t be written in any book but it still honors us as no less than kings.

You might scorn me but what I did, was something of a dream come true. To have been of use to someone dear to me. It felt as if the purpose of my life had met. So please, don’t be sad, for I am happy. I now live in your happiness. So if you want me to enjoy, and if you miss me, find happiness in life, take as many chances to avail and discover the wonders. That is where you will feel me living along with you. After all, remember, we promised to do everything together.

The great man once said, “A soul lost in life saving another soul, is a soul that has found eternity.” I lived a simple life but it was worth it. My time with you was when I felt alive. In this simple life you were the sunlight that helped me grow.

To be honest, my mind was filled with how am I even going to fit all in that I want to write, but now I do not even know what else to add, Hahaha, guess I am at a loss of words. I couldn’t even finish the story I started, You said you did not like it right. Guess you jinxed it.

I guess I never told you but my late father had a will. He wanted me to buried alongside him. He had booked the area along his grave for me beforehand. Though I did not really wanted to, I guess spending time with him like this might be enough to fulfil all the missing time from this life haha.

Oh, and don’t you dare call me selfish for making this decision all on my own. And now you must also be wondering that I have abandoned you. But look around, I leave you someone, a friend who I’m sure will be able to care for you second only to me.

By the way, the pen I am writing with is about to run out, just like me lol. But well, I said all the main things, lastly I shall say, “Live fully for the sake of both of us.”

Your Sweet,

Lil Sal.

Saiph had read that aloud. It was rather unexpected and I think he did it subconsciously. But I guess it could be because Sal wanted me to hear those words. As if giving me the role to look after him now that he was gone.

The note in itself was very simple. I expected more to be honest. Nevertheless, tears started dripping from his eyes and I realized, a letter that could make someone cry is never an ordinary one. But then again, a letter written to someone is not the same to some else too. I went ahead and held Saiph to give him some support but all he did was cry. Eventually he stopped. He tried to regain composure because his family was also in the room. He got up, hugged me, and that was the time that made me want to cry too but all I did was let out a single tear. He parted ways back to his house to fight his demons.

The following night, I went to Saiph’s home for mine was too silent for me and it was like fire to my internal negativity. At Saiph’s house. At least there was moving life. The night when I slept. I had the same dream again. I would crown Saiph, and people would chant for him. But to my surprise, the dream did not end this time. Saiph spoke in a loud voice. “I stand before you all today, no thanks to another person. A life who shone brightly enough to enlighten our whole kingdom. And because I owe my life to him, I will take the role, not alone but by his side.” Sal appeared out of nowhere, dressed mighty in a golden armor and a red velvet cape. He looked very handsome and mature. Saiph picked the crown from his head, and put it on Sal’s to which the crowd went chanting, “All hail King Sal.”

The ceremony was followed by a feast where somehow Kamilla showed up, and she asked me, “How does it feel to be an average human Mr. ex-King.” Suddenly I realized, this was my kingdom which I gave to Saiph who then gave it to Sal. For once, in the very same day, the kingdom of Saturn had three kings one after the other. It was indeed a day to be remembered.

The dream was so real that it made me open my eyes. I looked at the clock on the table besides me. ……….

20 Years later

Now that was a refreshing Sleep. Totally unlike all the night over I have had with Saiph back in the old days. Being nostalgic over the past, it felt very quick that 20 years had passed to those days. Camilla, who I used to call Maha now, turned towards me and said, “The very you used to complain about time being slow, no right do you have sir to say that it went by in a blink.”

While she was looking at me, I could only see and think, life was so beautiful. I had almost fulfilled all my dreams. The girl of my dreams laid besides me on the same bed looking as beautiful as ever.

I went to Japan more than twice now within this decade. I had a grand piano in my house that was able to play as well. I was able to buy the dream car, Audi E-tron GT just last year. The restaurant business that I always wanted to do was ever so booming. My mother was proud of me. And I had an amazing talented son named Jellal.

For 10 years now, I haven’t talked to Saiph. Neither seen him but today, the day had come. “You should get ready” Maha said, to which I replied, Daijobu. Giving me a look that spoke ‘seriously, at this age, still….’ I couldn’t help but respond, I am still a kid inside, don’t judge me.

“Kids aren’t as perverted as you are. Please.” Maha scoffed.

“Nothing wrong with being a little pervert with one’s own wife now is it.” I smirked at her.

“don’t set a loose example for your son.” She lightly criticized.

“Nothing wrong with teaching him to be a little romantic now is it!” I said while taking cloths out of the wardrobe.

“romantic hmmm, are you now.” She said giving a long look.

“Don’t compare an ordinary persons romance to the likes of a greedy woman like you.” Closing the wardrobe, I said having looked her one more time.

With a small silence, followed a light laughter by both of us. I was living a happy life.

It was a big mansion. “Dr.Saiph-ur-Rehman Cheema” written outside on the family name plate. Unlike how the morning started in the Rajeel mansion, Saiph woke up silently. His wife woke up too at the same time. They exchanged their mornings and got up in a decent manner. These people had a gentle start to their evening.

During breakfast, both Saiph and his wife sitting uptight and taking their food. The silence was only broken when Saiph asked, “You remember we have to go there right?”

“Yes, and I have taken out your dress as well. Change into it once you are getting ready.” Sophia replied. She gave the aura of a composed, collected woman.

Saiph a few minutes later again broke the silence by asking her. “Why didn’t you wake her up?”
“Let the child sleep Saiph, I will wake her up when I have to.” Sophia replied in a governing manner.

Life was like always. Silent and dignified.

Saiph too was now a successful doctor. That was the only dream I ever heard him say so I guess he achieved his dreams too. He had made tons of money and I guess for a Cheema, that was dream life.

It was the same house where I used to live with Sal 20 years ago. At that time my memories here were short but now, I had a whole bunch of them. I had decorated the house in a way that it gave a modern vibe while keeping alive the original theme of the house it was 20 years ago.

The day was 1st January, 2037. It was Sal’s birthday. It was the same day me and Saiph decided to meet exactly after 10 years having achieved the main targets of one’s life. This was the site where the pact was made.

The bell rang, me and Maha went to receive the gate. I opened it. The feeling of having to get to see your friend after 10 whole years standing tall, strong dignified just like a king was so overwhelming. I looked at the woman who was standing beside him and nodded with a gesture of tipping my hate and bowing down like they did in old English films. It was my first time meeting her.
Having received them, we headed inside. There was a weird frivolous tension in the air. The joint meeting was followed with introductions. Obviously Maha, me and Saiph were aware of each other so we took a while to get to know the wife of Saiph. Sophia Beghum.

After that I called Jellal down saying, “I present to you the prince of Saturn, Jellal Ali.”

I winked at Saiph hinting him that the bet we made 10 years ago that I won’t name my kid jellal, he had now lost.

“Then I present to you the princess of Saturn, Salia Cheema.” Saiph said. His wife was quite shocked to see Saiph using these words and manner but she spoke nothing. A pretty girl with a dark toned skin and chocolate color hairs stepped up. She looked quite graceful for a girl her age.

Sal…ia… I understood the weird sounding name and just laughed to myself in the head.

Eventually, both our wives were familiarizing among themselves, both our kids were getting to know each other better and me and Saiph, we headed up to the room that once belonged to Sal.

Nothing much was needed to be said here. It was a reunion of the people who shared the crown on the same night. Exchanging smiles, they raised their glass, “TOAST” to the reunion of the 3 kings.
